https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/ceqe.text: Image source, Reuters By Brandon Drenon Reporting from Washington DC Published 16 August 2026 The top US military commander in the Middle East has said mental health is a "priority" on the warship USS Lincoln, following reports of difficult conditions on board the long-deployed ship. After visiting the vessel on Saturday, Adm Brad Cooper said it had "among the lowest number of cases related to mental health" out of 11 active US aircraft carriers. But he acknowledged that Navy service at sea for long periods was "uniquely challenging and tough". The ship arrived in the Middle East in January and has been supporting the US war against Iran, including the blockade on Iranian ports. It has spent a record-setting uninterrupted time at sea of more than 240 days. Image source, EPA/Shutterstock The USS George Washington is reportedly heading to replace the USS Lincoln and could arrive in the region in about a week. Family members of sailors aboard the Lincoln have expressed concern about their mental health deteriorating due to the conditions, with some sailors having reportedly attempted to jump overboard. Adm Cooper said in a statement on Sunday: "I've long believed that mental health is another aspect of individual health and requires our attention just like physical health and spiritual health. "I applaud Lincoln's leadership for... stepping up and making mental health and crew resilience a leadership priority." While the US Navy last week acknowledged supply challenges, it had denied a mental health crisis on the Lincoln, which has 5,000 people aboard. Conditions aboard the ship have included poor sanitation, infrequent ports-of-call, broken plumbing and shortages of fresh food, according to reports last week in the Military Times and Stars & Stripes. Thirteen Democrats on the Senate Armed Services Committee sent a letter on Saturday to Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, criticising the length of the deployment as "a modern-day record" and demanding answers. Last week, Hegseth called reports of conditions "completely misrepresented", while President Donald Trump dismissed suggestions the sailors had been at sea too long, telling reporters on Friday: "Not nearly long enough." The USS Lincoln deployment, which was originally set to end in May, has been repeatedly extended. The personnel have reportedly been at sea without a port call for over 200 consecutive days. Maryland's Democratic Governor Wes Moore, a US Army veteran, told CNN on Sunday that the reported conditions were "heartbreaking" and the Republican president should have "more compassion". If you have been affected by any of the issues raised in this story you can visit BBC Action Line . Help and support outside the UK can be found at Befrienders Worldwide , external or you can call the US Suicide and Crisis Lifeline on 988. https://www.euronews.com/2026/09/09/temp.text: An explosion at a weapons depot near the northwestern city of Idlib killed at least 14 people and injured 11 others, Syria's Health Ministry said."The toll from the explosion in a temporary storage for collecting weapons and war remnants near the town of Sarmada ... registered 14 killed and 11 injured in a preliminary count," the Idlib health department said.Security forces cordoned off roads leading to the Burj al-Nimra area on the road to Sarmada, some 45 kilometres from Idlib, as Civil Defence and Syrian Red Crescent first-responders continued to search for survivors trapped under the rubble.Video footage widely circulated after the blast showed a large plume of black smoke and smaller explosions could be heard.The depot was used to store weapons and munitions left over from the country's civil war from 2011 until 2024, according to authorities.The cause of the blast near the town of Sarmada was not immediately clear. Initial assessments indicated the explosion was caused by munitions, said the head of emergency operations for Idlib's disaster management directorate, Walid Aslan.Ahmad Faour, a mechanic who works near the warehouse, said he and others first heard a small explosion and ran away before the large blast."A weapons warehouse should not be placed in a public area, in a village with people and shops," he said, after looking through the damaged cars in his garage. "Those poor people who died were not guilty of anything."The incident on Wednesday is the second deadly blast in Idlib this month, after a car carrying ammunition exploded, killing five in the city of Binnish.A government source said at the time that the car was owned by a weapons trader, while authorities did not announce the cause of the blast.Remnants of warSyria is ranked among the world's most heavily contaminated countries for unexploded ordnance.Explosions involving munitions-laden cars or arms depots have sporadically occurred in Idlib, a former front-line province where multiple armed factions stored weapons throughout the civil war which is among the most severely affected areas.In November 2025, a blast at an ammunition depot in the Kafr Takharim area killed five workers and wounded nine.In August 2025, an ammunition explosion on the outskirts of Idlib city killed four people and wounded five.Humanitarian organisations called on Wednesday for intensified international and local efforts to clear mines and war remnants from the province, which they said continued to claim Syrian lives on a recurring basis.UK mine-clearance charity HALO Trust estimated that this year unexploded ordnance was killing or wounding one person in Syria every six hours on average.By August, some 700 casualties from explosive accidents were recorded, one-third of them deadly and one-third being children, according to Simon Jackson, HALO Trust's Syria programme manager.According to Jackson, last year saw "a large spike in accidents as people rushed back to their communities" after the fall of al-Assad in December 2024.

https://www.digi24.ro/stiri/externe/ue/r.text: Apartenența Finlandei la NATO nu e pe masă, ca parte a unui potențial acord de pace pentru a pune capăt războiului purtat de Rusia în Ucraina, a declarat, vineri, ministrul A părării de la Helsinki. Rusia cere închiderea tuturor bazelor NATO din statele baltice, precum și retragerea completă a Finlandei din alianță, potrivit unei liste de revendicări obținute de ziarul german Bild . „Astfel de chestiuni nu sunt în niciun caz subiect de negociere”, a declarat ministrul finlandez al A părării, Antti Häkkänen, la Helsinki. „Rusia știe asta. Este absolut scandalos să sugerezi așa ceva”, a adăugat el, potrivit postului local de televiziune Yle . Timp de decenii, Finlanda a optat să rămână în afara NATO pentru a se adapta sensibilităților Rusiei. Cu toate acestea, după invazia la scară largă a Ucrainei de către Rusia la începutul anului 2022, conducerea politică a Finlandei a rupt linia de neutralitate și s-a alăturat alianței în aprilie 2024. Ca parte a acordului de pace, Rusia cere, de asemenea, ca Ucraina să nu se poată alătura niciodată NATO și recunoașterea internațională a controlului rusesc asupra teritoriilor ocupate, inclusiv Donbasul - în prezent, încă deținut parțial de Ucraina. În loc să se conformeze cerințelor Rusiei, Europa ar trebui să își dubleze sprijinul pentru Ucraina, a sugerat Häkkänen. „Cu cât Occidentul este mai blând față de ambițiile militare ale Rusiei, cu atât Rusia va testa din ce în ce mai mult”, a spus el. Reacțiile Finlandei vin după ce europenii s-au chinuit să prezinte un front unit în cadrul discuțiilor de pace reluate dintre Ucraina și Rusia la Abu Dhabi, mediate de SUA. Emisarii americani pentru pace au cerut europenilor să se implice mai mult în acest proces. Liderii UE sunt reuniți în prezent la Dublin pentru a discuta despr e, printre altele, cine ar trebui să reprezinte blocul comunitar în discuțiile viitoare.
